newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Metals - Zinc arriving shortly in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals - Zinc arriving shortly in Singapore.

text.p: Some 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes of Chinese zinc is due to arrive in Singapore shortly while another 5,000 tonnes is said to be bound for the city-state, regional traders said on Thursday.
"I think the zinc is arriving soon. They're preparing the space in the warehouses," the zinc dealer for a Japanese trading house told Reuters.
A European dealer estimated that "about 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes of zinc should be here soon" and some 5,000 tonnes would probably sail for Singapore over the next few weeks.
Some of the zinc will be stored in the Singapore warehouse of the London Metal Exchange (LME) while the others would remain off warrant.
Zinc prices on the LME recently hit a 4-1/2 year high above US$1,300 a tonne. The metal was indicated late on Wednesday in London at $1,280/84 a tonne.
Three-month zinc was being quoted by Far East traders at 0200 GMT little changed at $1,280/83 a tonne.
Metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review that technical selling may see zinc prices falling further.
"The correction could have further to run with a move to $1,250 now possible," Brandeis said.
Despite that prospect, Chinese sellers still find zinc prices attractive, traders said.
"I think they still like the prices," one zinc dealer said.
The Chinese are also trying to lift 3,000 to 5,000 tonnes of copper from the LME warehouse here.
"The Chinese are looking for copper but they'd want a cash price of $2,350 and below. The cash price is hovering above $2,400," a dealer for a European metal trading company said.
But another senior metal dealer in Hong Kong said the bulk of Chinese buying had not yet been seen by the market.
"I would think most of the buying will be in April/May," he said, adding buyers would be closely watching copper futures in Shanghai.

Traders estimate about 20,000-25,000 tonnes of copper is likely to be moved from the LME warehouse in Singapore to China. The volume of copper in the LME's singapore warehouse reached 42,875 tonnes in its stocks report last Tuesday against 55,000 tonnes in the LME stocks report on March 14, a fall of 12,125 tonnes.
Most of the stuff was believed to have gone to China, traders said.
Base metal trading in the rest of the region was largely dull ahead of the long Easter holidays, dealers said.
"It's holiday time," a European metal dealer said. "Starting on Wednesday, trading became flat."
Three-month copper prices were seen by the trade at 0200 GMT at $2,347/52 a tonne, slightly up from the late quote in London yesterday of $2,340/44 a tonne.
Aluminium was seen by the same dealers at 0200 GMT at $1,635/39 a tonne compared with the close in London on Wednesday of $1,632 a tonne.
Premiums quoted by dealers in Singapore were also unchanged to slightly higher, reflecting the dull mood of players ahead of the holidays, dealers said.
